key_moments.title: HEALTHCARE TRIAGE
A study published in the beginning of September 2020 examined 489 patients who had their Vitamin D level measured in the year before they were tested for Covid.
They found the RELATIVE risk of testing positive was 1.77 times greater for patients with "likely" deficient Vitamin D status.
Another study published later in September 2020 reported an association between Vitamin D level and clinical outcomes in 235 hospital patients.
One of the studies, published in the summer of 2020, found no correlation between Vitamin D level and confirmed Covid cases in a sample of over 500,000 participants.
We have NO evidence showing that Vitamin D levels directly impact susceptibility to or clinical outcomes of Covid-19.
Vitamin D, among its other roles, is known to play a supporting role in the response to viral infections.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials examining Vitamin D supplementation and risk of acute respiratory tract infection did find a positive effect.
Studies examining "low" Vitamin D levels often use cutoff points that aren't usually seen in healthy people.
Supplements are very poorly regulated in the United States, so it's generally hard to know what you're getting.
